newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland Elect accepts MMC price report.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland Elect accepts MMC price report.

text.p: Regional electricity company (Rec) Northern Ireland Electricity (NIE) on Friday welcomed the Monopolies and Mergers Commission pricing report but said it would resist any attempts by regulator Ofreg to make changes.

"The MMC agreed with much of NIE's case and rejected the DG's proposals. It is not now open to the DG to reject the MMC's conclusions and we shall resist any attempt on his part to do so," NIE said in a statement.

NIE said the review of its price controls has taken almost two years. It had rejected Ofreg director general Douglas McIldoon's original proposals and asked for the matter to be reviewed by the MMC. NIE said it had always made clear it would accept the MMC's findings.

McIldoon said he largely accepted the MMC's proposed modifications but wanted to make adjustments in respect of how the Commission determined the net present value of the rec's transmission and distribution (T&D) business.

"The DG's clear desire to challenge the process still further prolongs uncertainty and creates the risk that the regulatory framework will fall into disrepute," said NIE chief executive Patrick Haren in the statement.

The MMC recommended that NIE's transmission and distribution business charges be reduced by 25 percent in real terms in 1997/98 compared with 1996/97, and be cut by RPI minus two percent in each of the four subsequent years.
NIE had proposed a reduction of 22 percent while Ofreg had sought a cut of 33 percent.
The MMC also recommended NIE's supply business charges be reduced by 42 percent in real terms in 1997/87, and by RPI minus two percent in each of the next four years.

"The MMC's recommendations imply an overall reduction in NIE's component of electricity charges of 28 percent in real terms in 1997/98, compared with 1996/97. This compares with a reduction of 33 percent proposed by the director general," NIE said.
Haren said it provided a much fairer balance between the interests of customers and shareholders, and supports NIE's earlier decision to reject Ofreg's original proposals.

As well as representing a "very good deal for customers" Haren said implementing the recommendations will mean that NIE's charges for transmission, distribution and supply to domestic customers will be fully in line with its closest comparable Recs.
"The only obstacle to fully comparable prices lies with the generation contracts which result in generation costs being 30 to 40 percent higher in Northern Ireland," he said.
In its report the MMC also agreed with NIE's view that additional capital expenditure is required to improve the quality of supply to customers in rural areas, NIE said.
